headline.note: Cost you can save is price-only — what FDC overpaid this year versus the cheapest price it already paid for the same items (every material bought from 2+ vendors). Cash you can free is one-time working capital, released by moving suppliers off advance/immediate terms onto 30-day credit (annual spend × 30/365) — a different kind of money, never added to the cost saving.

actions.action: Use Sayaji Industries's lower price to push Gujarat Ambuja Exports down — don't just move more volume to Sayaji Industries.
actions.why: You pay Gujarat Ambuja Exports ₹68.5/kg for Dextrose Anhydrous IP (EXMPT); Sayaji Industries sells the same at ₹66.6/kg. But Sayaji Industries is already your biggest Dextrose source on a thin ~1% net margin — adding volume there deepens single-source risk. Use that gap to get Gujarat Ambuja Exports (30-day credit, stronger financials) down to it, or split to a second healthy source.
actions.risk: Sayaji Industries is already your biggest Dextrose source — keep its price as leverage, not a bigger basket.

actions.action: Put Tetrapak on 30-day credit — today it's pay-on-receipt.
actions.why: Tetrapak is your largest supplier on weak terms: you pay on the day goods arrive — no credit at all, while your other big suppliers already give you 30 days. On ₹5.46 Cr of spend, securing 30-day credit frees about ₹44.9 L of working capital — a one-time cash release, not a price cut. Sukhjit Corn Products is on even worse terms — 100% advance — but far smaller spend (₹1.06 Cr).

actions.action: Use Mars Plastics's lower price to push Cincorp International down — verify Mars Plastics before moving volume.
actions.why: You pay Cincorp International ₹1.08/pc for PP CAP PLAS 28MM INDUCTUCTION WAD; Mars Plastics quotes the same at ₹0.81/pc — a real price gap to lean on in your next review with Cincorp International. But Mars Plastics's financials aren't verified yet, so qualify it (health, supply continuity) before shifting volume — we don't vouch for a supplier we can't back.
actions.risk: Mars Plastics's financials are pending verification — use its price as leverage now; move volume only once it's vetted.
